guideTitle: 5 Best Pot and Pan Protectors in 2026
metaTitle: Best Pot and Pan Protectors in 2026
metaDescription: Five felt and fabric pot and pan protectors compared by size range, piece count and thickness, so stacked nonstick and enamel cookware stays scratch free.
introParagraphs: Stacked cookware is a reliable way to scratch a nonstick surface or chip enamel. Every time a skillet slides into another one, the base of the top pan rubs the cooking surface of the pan below it. Pot and pan protectors are soft separator pads that sit between the pieces so the metal never touches, and the five sets here cover a range from a short pack of three to a generous pack of twelve.

The sets differ in ways that are easy to miss in a thumbnail. The BOYAN pack includes 12 pads in sizes of about 10, 14 and 15 inches, the BYKITCHEN set stretches the diameters to 12, 14 and 16 inches, the VANWYCHEN set also gives 12 pads in the 10 to 15 inch range, and the KITLAB set uses four sizes from 10 to 16 inches with three pads each. The All-Clad pack goes the other way, with 6 pads in a thicker, branded fabric.

We evaluated these from the product pages and maker specifications, with attention to pad diameter, thickness, material and how many pads you actually receive. Nothing here claims hands-on trials, and the aim is to match the right set to the cookware you really own.

products.name: BYKITCHEN Felt Pot and Pan Protectors, 12 Piece
products.description:
The BYKITCHEN set is built around thickness. The maker describes its felt as heavy duty polyester that is thicker than common non-woven pads, which matters because a thin pad flattens under the weight of a stack and lets the rims touch. With 12 pads split into three sizes of 12, 14 and 16 inches, four of each, it covers the most common skillet, saute pan and stockpot diameters in a home kitchen.

The star shaped cutouts help the pad lie flat and give you a place to grip when you pull it out from between pans. The felt is described as washable and reusable, so a greasy pad can go through a wash rather than the bin. The tradeoff is that the smallest size is 12 inches, so tiny sauce pans of about 8 inches will have a pad that overhangs, which is harmless but a little untidy in a drawer.

Against the BOYAN pack, which starts at about 10 inches, this set suits cooks who own larger cookware, since its largest pad is 16 inches against the 15 inches of the BOYAN. Against the All-Clad, it gives twice the number of pads in the box. It is the best balance of count, size range and thickness in this lineup, and it is the set we would suggest for a typical family cookware collection.
products.bestFor: Large skillets and a family cookware set.
pros: Felt is thicker than common pads
Four pads in each of three sizes

products.name: BOYAN Felt Pot and Pan Protectors, 12 Piece
products.description:
The BOYAN 12 piece set is the one to choose if your drawer holds a good many small and medium skillets. Its smallest pad is about 10 inches, which fits an omelet pan or a compact skillet properly instead of hanging off the edges. The other two sizes of 14 and 15 inches cover mid sized frying pans and larger saute pans.

The listing says it is meant for protecting pots, pans, skillets, bowls and bakeware, and for creating a soft barrier that reduces scratches, scuffs and clanking between nested cookware. That broader use is genuine: the same pad works between plates, glass bowls and baking dishes. The cutting size means the 14 and 15 inch pads are close to each other, so you really get two big sizes that are not very different from each other.

Compared with the BYKITCHEN set, the BOYAN trades the 16 inch size for a smaller 10 inch one, so it suits a kitchen with compact cookware better than one with big stockpots. It does not make a claim about thickness, so it reads as a standard felt option rather than a premium one. If you cook for one or two people and your pans are modest in size, the BOYAN is the better fit.
products.bestFor: Small and medium skillets in compact kitchens.
cons: Top two sizes are close together
No thickness claim on the listing

products.name: VANWYCHEN Soft Felt Pan Protectors, 12 Piece
products.description:
The VANWYCHEN set is pitched on grip. The listing calls the felt pads non-slip, and the point is that a pad which stays put between pans makes stacking much steadier than a slick sheet that slides sideways. This matters when you lift a tall stack out of a low cabinet and one sloppy pad could let the whole tower shift.

The pads are made of lightweight polyester felt that the maker describes as eco-friendly and resistant to getting wet. With 12 pieces in sizes of 10, 14 and 15 inches, the lineup is the same size set as the BOYAN pack, so the choice between them comes down to material feel and the non-slip claim. The felt is soft rather than structured, so a pad can curl at the edges if it is folded for long.

Next to the BYKITCHEN, which markets its felt as thicker, the VANWYCHEN seems lighter, and that suits storage in a shallow drawer where bulk adds up. It also costs you nothing to use the pads for plates or bowls. For people who stack in a deep drawer and worry about slipping, this is a sensible choice, though thick cast iron or very heavy stockpots would be better served by the heavier felt of the BYKITCHEN.
products.bestFor: Tall stacks that tend to slide.
cons: Soft felt can curl at the edges

products.name: KITLAB Extra Thick Pot and Pan Protectors, 12 Piece
products.description:
The KITLAB set stands out because it offers four sizes rather than three. The 10, 12, 14 and 16 inch pads, three of each, spread across the whole range of a normal cookware collection, so no pan ends up with a pad that is far too big or too small. That is an advantage over the BYKITCHEN, which skips the 10 inch size, and over the BOYAN, which skips the 12 inch one.

The listing calls the pads extra thick and describes them as protecting pots, pans and ceramic dishware from scratches. Extra thickness is a practical benefit when you stack heavy items, since a thin pad compresses and loses its cushioning. It also makes the pads a little bulkier to store when they are not in use, so a very full drawer may feel tight.

In use, three pads per size means that you can protect a stack of four pans of the same diameter, which is enough for most households. If you routinely stack more than four of one size, the 4 per size sets such as the BYKITCHEN give you one more. For a cook with a varied set of pans and ceramic bakeware, the four size spread of the KITLAB is the most tailored choice in the comparison.
products.bestFor: A mixed set with many pan diameters.
pros: Extra thick pads hold their shape
cons: Bulkier to store than thin felt

products.name: All-Clad Professional Pot and Pan Protector Set, 6 Piece
products.description:
The All-Clad set is the premium brand pick, built for people who own expensive cookware and want matching accessories. It contains 6 pads made from a soft, thick and flexible polyester blend, finished in black and gray, and the listing describes sizes that are meant to fit different cookware shapes.

The benefit is a denser fabric that is meant to provide gentle cushioning, with a more finished look than basic felt discs. The tradeoff is count: with 6 pads, you get half as many as the 12 piece sets, so it is better suited to a core set of skillets and saucepans than a large collection. The listing does not give exact diameters in the text we reviewed, so check the product page against your largest pan before buying.

Against the BYKITCHEN, which gives twice the pads in thick felt, the All-Clad costs more per piece and gives you a branded finish. It makes sense if you own a clad stainless set and want the same name on the pads, or if you give a set as a gift. For pure value, one of the 12 piece sets is a better buy.
products.bestFor: A small clad set or a gift.
pros: Short set is easy to store
cons: Only six pads in the set
Exact sizes not stated in the text

buyingCriteria.explanation: A pad should be about as wide as the pan it protects, or slightly wider, so the base never touches the pan below. The BOYAN and VANWYCHEN sets start at about 10 inches, the BYKITCHEN at 12 inches and the KITLAB at 10 inches with a 12 inch option. Measure the widest pan you own, including the flared rim, and pick a set whose top size is at least that wide. A pad that is too small leaves the rim of the upper pan exposed and defeats the purpose.

Thickness decides whether a pad still cushions after a few weeks under a heavy stack. The BYKITCHEN describes its felt as thicker than common non-woven pads and the KITLAB calls its pads extra thick, while thinner felt can flatten and let metal contact the coating. Thick pads take more room in a drawer, so weigh cushioning against space. If you own cast iron or heavy stainless, favor the thicker sets.

A set of 12 pads sounds generous, but the count per size is what matters. The BYKITCHEN and BOYAN sets give 4 of each size, the KITLAB gives 3 of each across 4 sizes and the All-Clad gives 6 pads in total. If you stack five pans of one diameter, you need at least five pads in that size, so check the breakdown rather than the headline count. Large households that stack many skillets of one diameter should favor the BYKITCHEN or BOYAN packs, where four pads share each size.

Most of these pads are polyester felt, which is washable and does not absorb odors as quickly as natural wool. The BYKITCHEN describes its felt as washable and reusable, and the VANWYCHEN as resistant to getting wet. Always dry a pad completely before placing it between pans, since a damp pad can trap moisture against a cast iron surface. Wash greasy pads by hand with warm soapy water.

A pad that slides makes a tall stack unstable. The VANWYCHEN lists a non-slip surface, and the BYKITCHEN uses a star cutout so the pad lies flatter and is easier to lift out. Round pads with no cutout are fine, but a notch helps you pull one out with two fingers. If you keep pans in a high cabinet, a stable stack is a safety matter as well as a scratch matter.

Most of these pads work with plates, glass bowls, ceramic dishes and bakeware as well as pans. The KITLAB listing mentions ceramic dishware and baking dishes, and the BOYAN mentions bowls and bakeware. If your fine china needs the same protection, a bigger set with more pads is better value than a small premium set like the All-Clad. A pad between two plates also quiets the clatter when you unload the dishwasher, which is a small bonus for a drawer that sits close to a bedroom.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size coverage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the diameters listed for each set, from the 10 inch low end of the BOYAN, VANWYCHEN and KITLAB to the 16 inch top end of the BYKITCHEN and KITLAB. A set that covers more of a typical cookware range scored higher. We also noted where a size gap could leave a pan with an ill fitting pad.

howWeEvaluated.title: Thickness and material
howWeEvaluated.description: We read the material descriptions for felt thickness, fabric blend and any extra claims such as non-slip or water resistance. Thicker felt ranked above thin felt for heavy stacks, but we recognized that bulk has a storage cost. We did not assume performance beyond what the maker states.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pad count and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how many pads each set includes and how they are distributed across sizes. A pack of 12 with 4 per size can protect more stacks than a pack of 6, and we weighed the premium for brand against raw quantity.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ease of use and care
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered cutouts for lifting, washability, and whether the pads can be used for dishes as well as pans. A pad that is easy to pull out and easy to wash is one you will actually use daily.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The BYKITCHEN leads on thickness and size reach, the KITLAB on the number of sizes, the BOYAN on small pan fit, the VANWYCHEN on non-slip grip and the All-Clad on brand finish. These strengths drove the badges, and every comparison relies on listing specifications, not hands-on trials.

howToChoose.intro: Thickness changes both cushioning and drawer space.

cards.label: Thick felt
cards.text: A thick pad holds its shape under a heavy stack, so cast iron and heavy stainless stay properly separated. The BYKITCHEN and KITLAB are the thickest in this lineup, and the All-Clad is also described as thick. The cost is bulk in a drawer. Choose thick if you stack heavy cookware or fragile ceramic.

cards.label: Thin felt
cards.text: A thinner pad packs flatter and costs less per piece, which suits light aluminum pans and shallow drawers. The BOYAN and VANWYCHEN lean in this direction, with the VANWYCHEN described as lightweight. The cost is less cushioning when the stack is heavy. Choose thin if your pans are light and space is tight.

howToChoose.note: If in doubt, step up to the thicker felt; extra bulk is easier to live with than a scratched coating.

faq.q: How do I choose between felt pads and fabric pads?
faq.a: Felt pads like the BYKITCHEN and BOYAN are inexpensive, washable and widely available, while a fabric blend such as the All-Clad offers a denser feel and a finished look. For most kitchens, felt is the sensible choice. Pick fabric only if you want a matching set or are buying a gift.

faq.q: How many protectors do I need?
faq.a: You need one pad between each pair of stacked pieces, so a stack of five pans needs four pads. A pack of 12 covers a good-sized collection, while the 6 piece All-Clad set suits a core set of cookware. Count your largest stacks before you decide.

The BYKITCHEN lists its felt as washable and reusable, and other felt sets are commonly handled the same way. Wash by hand in warm soapy water and let them dry flat. Do not put damp pads between pans, since trapped moisture can harm cast iron and some coatings.

faq.q: Do pan protectors work for glass and ceramic?
faq.a: Yes, several listings mention bowls, ceramic dishes and bakeware. The KITLAB mentions ceramic dishware and baking dishes, and the BOYAN mentions bowls. A pad between plates also reduces chipping and noise. Use a size that covers the full base of the dish.

Thicker pads cushion better under heavy stacks, but they take more room and cost more storage space. Light pans do well with standard felt. Heavy cast iron, ceramic and stainless justify the thicker options from the BYKITCHEN or KITLAB.

faq.q: What size should I buy for a 12 inch skillet?
faq.a: A 12 inch skillet measures wider across the rim than across the base, so go one size up. The 14 inch pads in the BOYAN, BYKITCHEN and VANWYCHEN sets all work well. A pad that is too small leaves the rim bare and can still scratch the surface below.

faq.q: Will the pads slip in a drawer?
faq.a: Smooth felt can shift when you slide a drawer open. The VANWYCHEN lists a non-slip surface to reduce this, and the star cutouts on the BYKITCHEN help the pad lie flat. For deep drawers, stack no more than a few pans high so the weight stays stable.
